Do you still need a website if people just ask AI?

Yes. AI tools don’t invent their recommendations. They read the web and name the businesses whose websites answer the question clearly. Your website is what they read, quote and link to.

  1. It’s the source AI quotes. ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google’s AI Overviews pull from pages they can read. If your prices, services and hours aren’t on your site, they quote a directory or a competitor instead.
  2. It’s where the decision happens. An AI answer gets you on the shortlist. People still click through to check you’re real: photos, reviews, prices and a way to book. That click lands on your website.
  3. It’s the one channel you own. Social platforms and AI tools change their rules all the time. Your site, your enquiries and your customer list stay yours.

What has changed is what a good website looks like: clear answers, fast pages, and structured data that both people and AI tools can read. That’s how I build them.

Can AI tools read your website?Run any page through my SEO & AEO scanner. It checks 60+ things search engines and AI assistants look for, then lists what to fix first.

Monitoring for your brand and your website

Two problems most businesses only discover when it’s already costing them: someone pretending to be them, and their website quietly breaking for Google or AI tools. Both checks below run live on real data. Try them now, then let me keep watch every day.

Brand protection

Scam Scanner

Paste a suspicious link, or a whole SMS, Messenger, Viber or email message. It checks 40+ phishing signals, the live page, domain age and DNS, and threat-intel feeds, follows any redirects, and explains the risk in plain language.

For your business: the same checks can be pointed at new domains that look like yours, so lookalikes are flagged early, before they’re used to trick your customers.

Check a link or message

Search & AI visibility

SEO & AEO Scanner

Paste any page URL. It reads the page the way search engines and AI assistants do, runs 60+ checks, and gives you an SEO score, an AEO score and a ranked list of what to fix first.

For your business: the same engine can check every page of your site on a schedule and tell you when something breaks for Google or AI tools, before it costs you traffic.

Scan a page
Want this watching your business every day?

I set up two scheduled checks. First, your key pages are re-scanned every week, and you get an alert if one stops working for Google or AI tools, for example a page accidentally set to noindex or a blocked AI crawler. Second, new domains that look like yours are flagged as they appear in public certificate and registration records, so you can act before they’re used against your customers. Alerts go to your inbox or Slack, with what was found and what to do next.

An Honest Word on Cost

Most of the job is making the tools work together

There's a lot of hype out there. AI and automation can genuinely save you time and money, but only when someone sets them up properly. I've seen plenty of businesses pay for tools they barely use, automate the wrong things, and quietly give up a few months later.

My job is to make sure that doesn't happen to you. I focus on the handful of changes that will actually move the needle for your business, set them up right, and skip the stuff that just looks impressive but doesn't earn its keep.

    • Domain-specific search tools purpose-built for legal case databases, academic content, or financial filings, with citation trails, not hallucinations
    • Data cleaning and enrichment pipelines that standardize messy inputs, fill gaps from external sources, and feed clean records into your downstream systems

    AI agents

    An assistant that does the work, not just talks

    A regular chatbot can only answer questions. An AI agent can also do the follow-through: read a new enquiry, check your calendar, add the customer to your records, and write the reply. It works inside the apps you already use, like your email, booking system or CRM, so nobody has to copy things across by hand. You stay in control: it only does the jobs you give it, and checks with you before anything important goes out.

    Healthcare · Northgate Family Clinic

    Local search and AI answers

    The situation

    The clinic had one generic Services page and a Google Business Profile listed as “Medical clinic”. Nothing on the site said whether it took new patients or which insurance it accepted, the two things people search for most.

    What I did

    • Changed the profile's main category to Family practice physician, added every service and the booking link, and matched the name, address and phone across 40+ directories.
    • Wrote a New patients page that answers the five questions the front desk hears all day (insurance, what to bring, wait times, languages, booking) in short, plain sentences an AI answer can quote.
    • Added MedicalClinic and Physician structured data with opening hours, accepted insurance and each doctor's profile.
    • Built one page per service and per area served, each with the real doctors and real appointment times, not copy-paste location pages.
    • Set up a review request after each visit, with replies written within two days.

    What to look for

    The AI answer repeats the New patients page almost word for word. That page was written to be quoted.

    Legal · Ramos Whitfield Employment Law

    Getting cited in ChatGPT and Perplexity

    The situation

    The firm ranked on Google for its own name, but when people asked AI tools about their situation, the answers cited two big directory sites and a competitor.

    What I did

    • Pulled 24 real questions from intake calls and Reddit threads, then checked each one in ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google's AI Overviews every month.
    • Rewrote practice pages answer-first: the short answer in the first two sentences, then the law, the deadline and the exceptions.
    • Added attorney bios with bar numbers, years in practice and published cases, so AI tools have a named expert to cite.
    • Got the attorneys quoted on legal Q&A sites and in local news, the kind of sources AI answers lean on.
    • Kept every page inside bar advertising rules, with the required disclaimers.

    What to look for

    Which prompts flipped from a competitor to the firm, and which ones still haven't. The report shows both.

    E-commerce · Loam Ceramics

    Technical SEO and product data

    The situation

    Every glaze colour created its own URL, so Google saw four copies of each product and ranked none of them well. There was no product data, so search results showed no price, stock or stars.

    What I did

    • Pointed every colour variant at one main product URL and cut the sitemap down to pages worth indexing.
    • Added Product, Offer and Review structured data pulled from the store's live data, so price and stock stay correct on their own.
    • Set up free Merchant Center listings so products show in Google Shopping without ad spend.
    • Fixed 38 broken internal links and gave each collection page a short, useful intro.
    • Compressed images and delayed loading of lower sections so mobile pages pass Core Web Vitals.

    What to look for

    The crawl count dropping is the good news: fewer, stronger pages instead of a thousand weak ones.

    Real estate · Harbor & Pine Realty

    A content plan for neighbourhood searches

    The situation

    The blog was generic posts like “5 tips for first-time buyers” that could sit on any agency's site, so they ranked for nothing and no AI tool had a reason to cite them.

    What I did

    • Mapped 12 neighbourhoods into guide pages, each linked to schools, commute, a monthly market report and the home value tool.
    • Wrote each brief from the questions buyers actually ask the agents, checked against what people search.
    • Added monthly tables of prices and days on market, dated, so AI tools can quote them with confidence.
    • Put each guide under the agent who sells in that area, with their recent sales there.
    • Set a monthly refresh so the numbers never go stale.

    What to look for

    The questions come before the keywords. That's what makes the page useful to a buyer and quotable for an AI tool.

    Email operations

    AI email triage and drafted replies

    Reads every inbound email, works out what it is, and sends it to the right place: sales leads into HubSpot, support issues into the helpdesk, spam archived. Replies are saved as drafts, never sent blind.

    Built to run in production

    • Each email is processed once, even if Gmail sends it twice
    • Names, phone numbers and account details are masked before the AI reads them
    • Unsure classifications go to a person instead of a guess
    • Failures retry with backoff, then post to your ops channel with the email ID
    GmailOpenAI / ClaudeHubSpotZendeskSlack
    E-commerce

    Abandoned cart recovery that respects consent

    Follows up on abandoned checkouts with a short email sequence, but stops the moment the customer buys, checks marketing consent first, and caps discounts so margins stay safe.

    Built to run in production

    • Rejects fake webhooks by checking Shopify’s signature
    • Never emails people who haven’t opted in
    • Discount only appears in the last email, with a per-customer cap
    • Waits survive restarts, so nothing is lost if the server reboots
    ShopifyKlaviyo (via API)Postgresn8n
    Brand monitoring

    Brand mentions with severity-based alerts

    Checks Google Alerts, Reddit and review sites for new mentions every 15 minutes, scores each one for sentiment and how serious it is, and only interrupts the team for the ones that need a response. Everything else lands in a daily summary.

    Built to run in production

    • Uses public RSS feeds, so no paid social API is needed to start
    • The same post is never alerted twice
    • Alert rules are set per severity, so the team isn’t pinged for every mention
    • The scoring prompt is versioned, so changes can be compared and rolled back
    Google Alerts RSSReddit RSSClaude / OpenAISlack
    CRM operations

    Clean CRM sync with enrichment and a dead-letter queue

    Takes new contacts from forms and imports, checks and cleans them, matches them against existing records, adds company details, and writes them to the CRM without creating duplicates. Bad rows are parked for review, not lost.

    Built to run in production

    • Upserts by a unique key, so re-running a batch never creates duplicates
    • Enrichment results are cached to keep API costs predictable
    • Invalid rows go to a review table with the reason, ready to fix and replay
    • Every write is logged with source, time and what changed
    WebhooksHubSpotApollo / People Data LabsAirtable
    Content operations

    Research-backed drafts with an editor in the loop

    Starts from a brief in Notion, researches what already ranks, and produces an outline and first draft with sources attached. An editor approves it before anything reaches the website, and it is only ever saved as a draft.

    Built to run in production

    • Every claim in the draft links to the page it came from
    • Statements without a source are highlighted for the editor
    • Nothing is published automatically, only saved as a WordPress draft
    • Uses your style guide and banned-words list on every run
    NotionSerpAPIClaude / OpenAIWordPress
    Finance operations

    Invoicing and polite chasing, with owner sign-off

    Creates the invoice when a project is marked done, sends friendly reminders at 3, 7 and 14 days, and stops the second payment arrives. Anything over 30 days goes to the owner before a final notice is sent.

    Built to run in production

    • An idempotency key stops the same project being invoiced twice
    • Reminders stop the moment Stripe confirms payment
    • Final notices always wait for the owner’s approval
    • Payments sync to Xero so the books match without manual entry

    Common questions
    How much does it cost to talk to you?

    Nothing. The consultation is free, and if we take your case, we're only paid if we recover money for you.

    Will my employer find out I called?

    No. What you tell us is confidential, and we never contact your employer without your permission.

    I signed something when I left. Can I still sue?

    Often, yes. Some agreements don't hold up, and some claims can't be waived. Send it to us and we'll read it.

    How long do I have?

    It depends on the claim. Some deadlines are as short as 180 days, so it's worth asking soon.

    Common questions
    Will it work on hilly land?

    Yes. We use pressure-compensating drippers, so trees at the top and bottom of a slope get the same water.

    What if I don't have electricity?

    We can fit a solar pump. Many of our farms in Tambunan run on solar.

    Can you help with grant paperwork?

    We can prepare the quotation and technical documents most agricultural grant applications ask for.

    Who fixes it if something breaks?

    We do. Every system has a two-year warranty and a technician who knows your farm.

    The problem

    A boutique fashion retailer was losing organic traffic and manually managing every customer touchpoint, abandoned carts, order confirmations, review requests. Their site had technical SEO issues, thin content, and no automation layer whatsoever.

    What I did

    • Technical SEO audit identifying crawlability gaps, duplicate content, and missing schema markup
    • AEO-optimized content clusters built around high-intent product and category keywords
    • n8n automation pipeline handling abandoned cart recovery, post-purchase sequences, and review solicitation
    • API integration connecting Shopify, their email platform, and Google Sheets into a single reporting view
